core_obligations: Choose a presentation of the finite module and write the Fitting ideal as the ideal generated by the maximal minors of the presentation matrix (proof lines 1369-1380).
Prove that the rank condition at a prime forces one of the minors to become invertible after localisation (proof lines 1381-1395).
Conversely, use an invertible maximal minor to exhibit the localised module as free of the expected rank (proof lines 1396-1410).
Conclude the equivalence stated in the lemma (proof lines 1410-1411).
proof_roadmap: Identify the Fitting ideal with the ideal of maximal minors of the chosen presentation (proof lines 1369-1380).
From the rank condition, deduce that a maximal minor is invertible at each relevant prime (proof lines 1381-1395).
From an invertible maximal minor, exhibit a basis of the localised module (proof lines 1396-1410).
difficulty_reason: The lemma relates the Fitting ideal of a presentation of a finite module to the locus where the module is locally free of a given rank, and its proof is a 43-line argument. It chooses a presentation, identifies the Fitting ideal as the ideal generated by the maximal minors of the presentation matrix, and then proves the two implications by localising: on the one hand a rank condition forces a minor to become a unit, on the other the invertibility of a minor exhibits the localised module as a free module of the expected rank. The two directions are carried out with explicit matrices, so the proof is a computation rather than a citation.
